cards.title: Harvard: value-based healthcare delivery curriculum
questions: How does Michael Porter define value-based healthcare?
How should patient outcomes and cost be linked in value-based care?
cards.summary: The Harvard curriculum frames value around patient health outcomes relative to the resources used to achieve them. Practice binding an explicitly defined patient population, outcome observation and cost period; a lower cost alone does not establish improved patient value. These are source-linked educational concepts and Agere-authored analytics exercises. Patient-specific diagnosis, treatment suitability and dosing still require applicable evidence and review.

cards.title: ACC HF in a Box: GDMT teaching deck
questions: Which ACC teaching slides discuss GDMT implementation and medication tolerability?
cards.summary: The ACC teaching deck discusses medication classes, sequencing and practical tolerability issues. Its selected slides distinguish target-dose discussions from individual blood-pressure tolerance and monitoring considerations. The Agere-authored analytics exercise is to assess documented class coverage and dose exposure separately, bind reasons to dated source evidence, and leave maximum tolerated dose unresolved when it is not documented. This is an attributed educational summary of selected slides, not an adopted patient treatment protocol.

facts.reading_scope: Selected slide text and references inspected, particularly slides 30-31 and 35-37; no claim of full visual or clinical adjudication.
facts.authored_analytics_exercise: Keep medication class coverage, dose exposure, documented tolerance and dated safety observations distinct.
